focus: Terminal versus desktop: whether a CLI or TUI can give the OpenBot app experience (conversations, approvals inbox, activity feed, routine list), which repos ship a terminal UI or desktop shell worth copying, and what a Tauri desktop shell adds that a terminal cannot.
noveltyJustification: 7 of 8 findings were fully new and 1 mapped the four app surfaces onto data sources established earlier.

label: OpenBot Desktop installs and runs OpenBot for one person on one computer with no terminal, developer tools or container engine of the person's own; it is standalone, has no organization sign-in and installs the default Bot.

Desktop can also connect to an OpenBot running elsewhere and show it in the app window, signing in with OAuth 2.1 authorization code plus PKCE and keeping the refresh token in the operating system's credential store.

Desktop updates itself with a signed updater: a bar or tray item offers the update, the feed is read at launch and every six hours, release images are downloaded in the background, and an upgrade takes a database dump and restores it if a step fails.
The Tauri shell is one resizable 1000x800 window with tray-icon, image-png, deep-link, shell and single-instance plugins, bundled as dmg, nsis, appimage, deb and rpm.

The terminal can render the four app surfaces from existing data: a conversation pane over the new conversation file, an approvals pane over bots inbox, an activity pane over the status index, and a routine list over BOT.md triggers and schedule state.

The closest liftable terminal reference is Turnstone's CLI, an Apache-2.0 TerminalUI with readline, a session protocol and workstreams; openhuman-tui is a richer conversation-first ratatui frontend but GPL-3.0 and therefore design reference only.

A desktop shell adds an embedded browser for the Bot's computer and handover, tray and OS notifications, global hotkey and deep links, the OS credential store, native file dialogs and a signed self-updater that installs and upgrades the stack; a terminal can approximate notifications but not the embedded browser or no-terminal install.

The recommended path is terminal first: a TUI with four panes over existing stores (size L), deferring a desktop shell (size XL) until the browser view, tray notifications or a no-terminal install become must-haves, because the desktop shell also adds a packaging, updater and container-engine surface.
